eda_observations.fact: The usable training schema contains integer play_time_ms, duration_ms, and long_view columns, together with tab, timestamps, user/video IDs, and auxiliary feedback.
eda_observations.implication: Test the official long_view definition against every training row and, if exact and both inputs exist in evaluation_features, reconstruct the label directly instead of estimating it. Exclude long_view itself from all inference inputs.

eda_observations.fact: Training has 5,055,984 rows, 983 users, 2,119,510 videos, and long_view prevalence 0.2634626613 over 2022-04-08 through 2022-04-21.
eda_observations.implication: Use vectorized columnar inference for the definition rule; any learned fallback must be bounded for multi-million-row training and evaluated with a chronological internal split rather than random row splitting.

eda_observations.fact: Validation has 2,524,980 rows and 1,159,803 unique videos; 0.7422197404 of validation rows refer to videos unseen in training.
eda_observations.implication: Do not lead with video-ID memorization or a direct port of the Pure FM. Learned fallbacks must derive most signal from row context, feedback, duration, and basic metadata that can transfer to unseen videos.

eda_observations.fact: Among 2,119,510 training videos, median frequency is 1, the 90th percentile is 4, and 0.6706248142 are singletons.
eda_observations.implication: Regularize or omit raw video-ID effects and smooth all author/music/tag aggregates; a model whose capacity is dominated by item embeddings is unlikely to transfer.

eda_observations.fact: The median user has 3,489 training rows (p90 11,662), while per-user long_view rates range from 0.0106666667 to 0.832 with median 0.3367752184.
eda_observations.implication: User-conditioned histories and user/context baselines have enough support to be credible fallbacks, but rate features must be smoothed for the few sparse users and constructed without same-row target leakage.

eda_observations.fact: Measured correlations with long_view are 0.7562633232 for is_click and 0.5800293906 for play_time_ms; profile entry and comment stay time are weaker, while is_hate is -0.0204780332.
eda_observations.implication: The nonlinear documented threshold should supersede linear proxy use. If exact reconstruction is unavailable, retain click, watch time, negative feedback, and other inference-available feedback as distinct features or auxiliary tasks rather than treating all engagement signals identically.

eda_observations.fact: Scenario mix and label rate vary sharply: tab 1 has 3,286,302 rows at 0.3194828108, tab 0 has 1,066,194 at 0.0395547152, and tab 4 has 402,534 at 0.4310815981; several tabs are very rare.
eda_observations.implication: Every learned fallback must include tab and tab-by-feedback/duration interactions, with pooling or smoothing for rare tabs rather than unconstrained tab-specific models.

eda_observations.fact: duration_ms ranges from 0 to 10,869,724, with median 29,866, p90 193,100, and p99 486,533.
eda_observations.implication: Implement the documented 18,000 ms threshold with integer comparisons, including zero-duration edge cases verified on training. Learned fallbacks should use capped/log duration and threshold-margin features rather than an unscaled raw duration alone.

eda_observations.fact: Daily long_view rate varies from 0.2487835377 on 2022-04-12 to 0.2872951041 on 2022-04-16 without a monotone trend.
eda_observations.implication: Do not extrapolate a simple global linear date trend. For learned models, preserve chronology, include calendar/time context, and favor recency weighting only as a predeclared refinement rather than an assumed improvement.

eda_observations.fact: Basic video metadata covers 4,371,868 unique videos and includes author_id, music_id/type, tag, upload attributes, video type, dimensions, and duration; author and music IDs are themselves very high-cardinality.
eda_observations.implication: For cold-video generalization, parse tags and low-cardinality content attributes, but smooth/hash high-cardinality author and music identifiers and always provide unknown buckets.

first_attempt: Deterministic target-definition reconstruction. It is first because the official KuaiRand definition gives an exact rule, the measured usable schema contains both required operands, it is invariant to the 74.2% cold-item rate, and a full-training equality assertion can falsify it before relying on a controller score. If valid, no learned family can rank positives above negatives more correctly.

evidence: Source:KuaiRand official repository README: data descriptions
portfolio.falsifier: Reject the family if the integer rule disagrees with even one non-null training label after explicit edge-case handling, if either required evaluation column is absent, or if a scored run that passes those checks reports GAUC below 1.0 beyond numerical tolerance.
portfolio.mechanism: The official target is a deterministic threshold of two allowed impression fields, so the binary rule play_time_ms >= min(duration_ms, 18000) should place every positive above every negative without statistical estimation, cold-start error, or temporal drift.
portfolio.resource_plan: Use a vectorized PyArrow/Polars/NumPy scan of only play_time_ms and duration_ms, emit finite float32 0/1 scores in source row order, and save a tiny versioned JSON checkpoint containing the threshold and comparison semantics. No fitting, GPU, or external data is required; the full-training equality check is deterministic verification.

portfolio.falsifier: Abandon the ranking-objective hypothesis if its controller primary does not exceed the applicable simpler/incumbent supervised checkpoint by the campaign's frozen epsilon, particularly when an nDCG@5 gain is offset by a GAUC loss.
portfolio.mechanism: If the documented rule cannot be used, boosted trees can learn nonlinear watch-time/duration, click, tab, time, user, and content interactions while a user-grouped LambdaRank objective emphasizes the top five positions. Smoothed content/context statistics can transfer where video IDs are unseen.
portfolio.resource_plan: Build only inference-available features: threshold margin/ratio when present, log/capped duration, feedback flags, tab and time fields, basic video attributes, tag hashes, unknown indicators, and leakage-safe smoothed user/tab/author/tag rates. Train one bounded CPU LightGBM ranker on a user-sorted view of the approximately 5.1M rows with at most 63 leaves and a fixed tree/early-stopping budget; persist the booster, encoders, aggregate tables, feature order, and original-row mapping.

evidence: Source:KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos
Source:Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
portfolio.falsifier: Reject this added complexity if its controller primary fails to improve on the cold-aware tree ranker/current incumbent by the frozen epsilon, or if bounded training cannot reproducibly finish and reload within the candidate resource limits.
portfolio.mechanism: Dense per-user histories can identify which prior content and feedback are relevant to the candidate. Candidate-conditioned attention over metadata-level behaviors should represent diverse interests better than one global user embedding while avoiding dependence on cold video IDs.
portfolio.resource_plan: Construct histories strictly from earlier training events and use the full training prefix for evaluation inference. Cap each history at the latest 128 events, use 16-32 dimensional embeddings for tag, hashed author, music type, video type, duration bucket, tab, feedback type, and recency, omit/mask raw video ID, and train at most two mixed-precision epochs on a deterministic per-user sample capped near 1.5M rows. Persist vocabularies, preprocessing constants, weights, and the frozen history store.

problem_summary: Rank the already logged standard-recommendation impressions within each user for future dates by long_view, preserving authoritative row order. The controller's arithmetic mean of GAUC and nDCG@5 is the only score. Validation labels, hidden-test data during research, the random-exposure log, and month-aggregated video statistics are unavailable. The central research finding is that the official KuaiRand data documentation defines long_view deterministically from two measured usable log fields, so exact definition reconstruction has higher expected value than fitting a probabilistic model; learned models are fallbacks only if a full training assertion or evaluation schema falsifies that transfer.

sources.claim: The official field definition states that long_view equals 1 when play_time_ms is at least duration_ms for videos no longer than 18,000 ms, or at least 18,000 ms for longer videos. It also defines both inputs in milliseconds and identifies tab as the interaction scenario.
sources.decision: Make a vectorized score equal to (play_time_ms >= min(duration_ms, 18000)) the first attempt, preceded by an exact full-training equality assertion and required-column check; preserve row order and checkpoint only the rule specification.
sources.limitations: This is dataset documentation rather than a model result. Exact transfer still depends on the campaign's sanitized evaluation_features retaining both fields with the same semantics, so it must be checked against all available training labels and the evaluation schema rather than assumed.
sources.title: KuaiRand official repository README: data descriptions

sources.claim: The primary dataset paper documents 12 feedback signals, rich user/item side information, thousands of interactions per user, multiple recommendation scenarios, and the suitability of KuaiRand for long-sequence and multi-task modeling.
sources.decision: If definition reconstruction is falsified, reserve one candidate for chronological multi-feedback user-history modeling with basic metadata, but do not add propensity/debiasing machinery because its identifying random-exposure data is unavailable here.
sources.limitations: The paper discusses the broader KuaiRand collection and emphasizes random exposure for debiasing; this campaign is a 1K standard-log future-impression ranking task and explicitly withholds the random log and aggregate video statistics. It does not establish a winning model on this split.
sources.title: KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos

sources.claim: LightGBM's official documentation says lambdarank_truncation_level controls the top-results focus, should generally be slightly above the desired NDCG cutoff (for example k+3), and that lambdarank_norm normalizes lambdas across unbalanced queries.
sources.decision: For the tree-ranking fallback, sort a training view by user, pass user-sized query groups, set objective=lambdarank, metric=ndcg, eval_at=5, lambdarank_truncation_level=8, and lambdarank_norm=true, while restoring original evaluation row order after prediction.
sources.limitations: LambdaRank targets NDCG rather than this campaign's equal GAUC/NDCG mean, and the users have unusually large and unequal impression groups. Its advantage over pointwise learning is therefore empirical, not guaranteed.
sources.title: LightGBM official parameter documentation: LambdaRank

sources.claim: The primary DIN paper argues that one fixed pooled user vector loses diverse interests and proposes a local activation unit that forms a candidate-specific representation by weighting relevant historical behaviors.
sources.decision: For the neural-history fallback, attend over at most the latest 128 prior events using candidate and history tag/author/music-type/video-type/duration-bucket features, mask or omit raw video ID, encode feedback type and recency, and compare it only after the cheaper context ranker.
sources.limitations: DIN was evaluated for CTR in advertising/e-commerce, not long_view on this split; unrestricted attention over thousands of events is expensive, and target item IDs cannot generalize to the measured 74.2% cold-item rows.
sources.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
